Alex Zhao: Heads up — Acme's procurement just sent a vendor risk request asking for our breach notification timeline and how we escalate to customers. They want specifics for POC contract.
Maria G: thanks. do we have a short blurb we can give them? they asked for SLA timelines + example notification wording.
Elaine (sales): They want to include it in the legal addendum for the pilot. quick answer is fine, legal will polish. key is notify within X and provide root cause within Y.
Devon Patel: For Hosted customers we have: initial acknowledgement within 24h of detection, prioritized customer notification within 48h if customer data impacted, detailed RCA and remediation plan within 30 days. For VPC/private customers we can offer tighter SLAs on a case-by-case.
Samira (security): Slight refinement: detection -> internal triage within 8h; customer notification timeline depends on impact severity. For Severity 1 (data exfiltration) we notify customers within 24h with recommended mitigations; for Severity 2 (exposure without confirmed exfiltration) notify within 72h pending analysis. Also note GDPR 72h regulatory window for supervisory authorities.
Alex Zhao: copy. can we give them a sample notification email they can include in the contract?
Samira (security): yes — short template below. include contact points, what we’ll provide (scope, timeline, mitigations), and offer a joint call. Also mention we’ll rotate POCs and provide logs.
Samira (security): ```Subject: Redwood Inference — Security Incident Notification
Hi <Customer Sec Team>,
We have detected a security event that may affect your data. Summary: <one-line summary>. Detection time: <UTC timestamp>. Impact: <systems/customers affected>. Immediate actions taken: <containment steps>. Expected next update: within 24/48/72 hours (depending on severity). Point of contact: security@redwood.ai and <account rep>. We will provide a full root cause analysis and remediation timeline within 30 days unless work-in-progress requires an extension.```
Elaine (sales): nice. can we attach CAIQ / SIG reference? Acme asked for the mapping to our IR controls.
Devon Patel: we have a one-page mapping: CAIQ section 9 + SIG question set IR-1..IR-5 -> our policies: incident response runbook, oncall, legal notify timeline, log retention. I can extract a short bulleted mapping.
Alex Zhao: will that live in Confluence or can we just paste a PDF? procurement prefers a PDF.
Samira (security): put PDF + canonical Confluence link. make sure it includes contact escalation matrix (security, legal, sales). Also confirm whether Acme requires regulator notification support — if so legal needs to review before we promise anything.
Elaine (sales): @Samira noted. I'll ask procurement whether regulator assistance is needed. For the POC contract we’ll send: (1) short timeline blurb, (2) sample email, (3) CAIQ IR mapping PDF, (4) point-of-contact list.
Devon Patel: FYI for on-call play: incident-bot will generate an incident ticket with runbook link; that ticket id can be included in customer follow-ups.
incident-bot: incident ticket #INC-2026-732 created, severity pending triage — runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ir/runbook
Maria G: perfect. Elaine — want me to draft the pack and send to you for review before legal?
Elaine (sales): please do. target EOD PST. :thumbsup:
Alex Zhao: thanks all. putting a short note in the CRM linking the docs so AE has everything during signature.
